root_cause.text: In the qla2xxx driver, module unload could proceed while a fabric/device scan was still active, so an interrupt-time scan completion path hit the UNLOADING check, skipped workqueue allocation, and freed DMA-mapped scan resources directly from IRQ context.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly states that during device discovery/fabric scan, setting the UNLOADING flag caused the work item not to be allocated and “the mapped memory had to be freed,” with the free (`dma_free_attrs`) occurring in interrupt context; the fix adds `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` to `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` so unload waits for scanning to finish.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit message explicitly states that during device discovery/fabric scan, setting the UNLOADING flag caused the work item not to be allocated and “the mapped memory had to be freed,” with the free (`dma_free_attrs`) occurring in interrupt context; the fix adds `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` to `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` so unload waits for scanning to finish.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make HBA readiness waiting include the active scan flag so the driver does not proceed while scanning is still in progress.
intent_record.what: The loop condition in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() was extended by adding an extra disjunct, '(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)', so the function now continues waiting not only during reset, mailbox busy, and FX00 reset/target-scan states, but also while the SF_SCANNING flag is set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will block longer and avoid treating the HBA as ready while a scan is still in progress, preventing execution from proceeding during an active scan state that was previously not considered by this readiness check.

grouping_result.intent: Make HBA readiness waiting include the active scan flag so the driver does not proceed while scanning is still in progress.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is unload/progress continuing while a scan is still active. This change explicitly makes readiness waiting account for the active scan flag, preventing operations from proceeding during an in-progress scan, which directly addresses that race.

candidates.rationale: This wait condition omitted the active fabric/device scan state, so the code could treat the HBA as ready and allow unload/progress while a scan was still running, which is the root cause described.

As part of the pre-fix readiness predicate, this line contributed to a loop that waited on reset/mailbox activity but not on an active scan flag, enabling unload to proceed during an in-progress scan.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix wait-loop condition checked reset, DPC, and mailbox activity but did not include the active fabric/device scan state. Because scan activity was omitted from the readiness gate, module unload could continue while a scan was still in progress, leading to the later IRQ-context scan completion path freeing DMA-mapped scan resources after hitting the UNLOADING check.

This line is part of the same pre-fix readiness predicate whose omission of the active scan flag allowed the driver to consider the HBA ready despite an ongoing scan. That missing condition is what enabled unload to proceed concurrently with scan completion, triggering the vulnerable IRQ-context cleanup path.
